name: Tata Capital Ltd
tagline: India's 3rd-largest diversified NBFC, compounding AUM ~22% and PAT ~50%+ — a quality franchise, but a genuine large-cap at ~Rs 1.55 lakh Cr trading ~4x book on a sub-peer ~1.9% RoA, with no specific named inflection to lift it out of size math
business_overview: Tata Capital (listed Oct 2025) is the third-largest and one of the fastest-growing diversified NBFCs in India, with a 100%-owned housing-finance subsidiary. It serves ~7.3 million customers across 25+ lending products spanning retail, SME and corporate. AUM ~Rs 2.9 lakh Cr as of Jun 2026.
fundamentals_table: ~20% AUM CAGR FY25-27E; ~34% PAT CAGR; RoA/RoE ~1.9% / ~13.2% (FY26E/27E)
~3.4-4.1x P/B vs peer avg ~3.7x; RoA ~1.9% vs peer avg ~3.0%; ~2.7x FY27 P/B on JM Financial's math
IPO Oct 2025 at Rs 330; flat debut; JM Financial 'ADD', ~9% upside
fundamentals_narrative: A high-quality compounder: 22% AUM growth (28% ex the run-down motor book), 56% PAT growth in Q1 FY27, Tata brand, AAA rating and a low cost of funds. But two things cap the return case. First, size: at ~Rs 1.55 lakh Cr market cap, a 10x would make it larger than the biggest Indian banks today, and 100x in a decade is arithmetically implausible — a genuine large-cap defaults to 'neither' on size math. Second, valuation: it trades at a premium to NBFC peers (~4x book) while earning a lower RoA (~1.9% vs ~3.0%), and brokers see limited near-term upside. There is no specific, named management or structural inflection (no turnaround CEO, no regulatory regime change) that would invoke the large-cap exception.
technical_read: Flat since its Oct 2025 debut; trades near the IPO band.
